Jon Rivera: Morning — first day! Quick q: I enabled FileVault on my Mac. For backups, is it OK to use iCloud for personal dev configs that accidentally include API keys? Where should I store FileVault recovery keys per policy? @Mira Patel
Mira Patel: Congrats, Jon! Short answer: do NOT keep company API keys in iCloud. Company secrets must go in 1Password/Secrets Manager. Personal configs can live in iCloud if encrypted and isolated from corp data. Recovery keys: if this is a company-managed device IT will escrow it; otherwise keep it in a private password manager entry. :thumbsup:
Jon Rivera: Cool — so I should rotate any tokens I accidentally put in my dotfiles and move them to 1Password. Who handles SSH key rotation — infra or me?
IT Support: Hi Jon — generate SSH keys locally and upload the public key to the infra repo/team page. For org-level access use your YubiKey for signing. We don't rotate personal dev keys automatically; infra rotates service keys. DM us if you want migration help.
Carla Nguyen: To add: treat backups of images/configs that contain creds as company secrets. Don't push them to personal cloud without scrubbing. If your device is enrolled, IT will escrow recovery keys into our KMS.
Jon Rivera: Device shows as "enrolled" in Jamf — I completed the flow. About phone MFA: do I need to enroll my personal phone in MDM to use SMS or Authenticator?
Mira Patel: Personal phone enrollment in MDM is optional. Use an authenticator app (Authy/1Password/Google Authenticator) for MFA. MDM on personal devices is only required for access to sensitive datasets or if you request certain internal VPNs. People Ops manages exceptions.
People Ops Bot: Reminder — complete "Security Foundations" training within 7 days to avoid escalation. Link: https://redwood.company/training/security-foundations
Jon Rivera: Thanks! One last Q: Docker images I build locally sometimes include creds in layers. Best practice is to scrub, build fresh, and push to internal registry with ephemeral creds, right?
Carla Nguyen: Exactly. Use build args sparingly, never bake secrets into images. If you need to share a dirty commit for debugging, use the secure file upload in the ticketing system or redact before sharing.
Jon Rivera: Awesome, that clears things up. Appreciate the quick responses — filing a ticket if I hit any migration hiccups.
